channel.title: PlanProof Insights
channel.description: Plain answers to the questions risk, compliance and audit teams ask about business continuity and crisis management exercises in the UAE.

item.title: Is your organization ready for the rainy season? A pre-season continuity checklist
item.description: Ready means five things are settled before the first orange alert: who decides to send people home and by when; what you will do when water reaches the basement, where many buildings keep their power, lifts and pumps; how you reach staff who cannot reach you; what your insurance actually covers and who photographs what; and one rehearsal of the whole thing with the people who would really decide. The forecasters say this winter could be wetter than usual. Nobody is promising a storm, but the checklist costs an afternoon and the alternative costs a week.

item.title: Flood insurance claims in the UAE: what is and is not covered, and why claims get declined
item.description: Comprehensive motor and home policies responded to the April 2024 floods; the central bank said so, and the motor policy’s natural-disaster exclusion never applied because no authority declared one; third-party motor cover never pays for your own vehicle. Claims were declined for what people did rather than for the weather: driving into a flooded road or underpass, restarting a car that had been in water, or claiming without photographs. Business-interruption cover usually needs physical damage to your own premises. Disputes go to the central bank’s ombudsman, then a disputes committee, whose decisions are not published. Two and a half years on, our search of the public court record found one ruling, about where a reinsurance dispute should be heard, and no judgment either way on a flood claim. This article describes what was reported; it is not legal or financial advice.

item.title: What does NCEMA 7000:2021 require for exercising and testing?
item.description: NCEMA 7000:2021 requires a planned exercise and test process with realistic scenarios, clear objectives, defined success criteria and a post-exercise report with recommendations, run at planned intervals and after any significant change. It does not name a type of exercise and it does not set a fixed frequency — those decisions are left to you, and you need to be able to justify them.

item.title: What should an ISO 22301 exercise programme contain?
item.description: ISO 22301:2019 (clause 8.5) asks for a programme of exercises and tests that is consistent with your scope and objectives, uses well-planned scenarios with clear aims, builds the team’s competence, validates the whole of your business continuity arrangements over time, produces formal post-exercise reports with actions, feeds continual improvement, and runs at planned intervals and after significant change. The word that matters is programme: a planned series that, taken together, covers all of your arrangements over time, rather than a single event.

item.title: Tabletop exercise or simulation: which one does the auditor expect?
item.description: Neither standard requires a particular type of exercise. What an auditor expects is a programme that is proportionate to your risks and, over time, validates the whole arrangement: evidence of objectives, a realistic scenario, a report, and closed actions. For most UAE organizations a sensible programme is a facilitated tabletop at least once a year (the standards set no frequency), a technical test wherever a plan makes a recovery promise, and a larger simulation only once the tabletops stop finding big gaps.

item.title: How do tabletop exercises prepare your team for better crisis management?
item.description: A tabletop exercise puts the crisis management team under a realistic scenario with a clock running, so they practise the three things a plan cannot do for them: deciding with incomplete information, communicating in the right order, and knowing who owns which call. The team that comes out of it is faster, calmer and clearer about roles. The gaps it finds can then be fixed before a real incident exposes them.

item.title: What does a readiness score tell a board — and what doesn’t it?
item.description: A readiness score tells a board, in one number, how well the team performed against a specific scenario on a specific day, where the weaknesses clustered, and — once there is a second exercise — whether things are improving. It does not tell the board the organization is safe, it does not cover risks that were not exercised, and it is not a certification. Used with those limits understood, it is the most useful single line in a continuity report.

item.title: The annual business continuity exercise checklist
item.description: An annual exercise runs all year: confirm last year’s actions are closed, pick this year’s risk and the plan it tests, set a date that avoids Ramadan hours, summer leave and year-end, write two or three objectives, brief the team, run the exercise with an observer, report within three working days, assign actions with owners, feed the management review, and keep the evidence pack together.
